{{nihongo|'''Funai Shrine'''|船井神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Yagi-chō Funaeda, {{ill|Nantan, Kyoto|ar|نانتان (كيوتو)|azb|نانتان، کیوتو|ce|Нантан|ceb|Nantan-shi|cs|Nantan|de|Nantan|es|Nantan (Kioto)|fa|نانتان، کیوتو|fi|Nantan|fr|Nantan|gl|Nantan|id|Nantan, Kyōto|it|Nantan|ja|南丹市|ko|난탄시|lt|Nantanas|my|နန်းတန်းမြို့၊ ကျိုတို|mzn|نانتان، کیوتو|nl|Nantan|pl|Nantan|ro|Nantan|ru|Нантан|sv|Nantan|tg|Нантан|th|นันตัง|tl|Nantan, Kyoto|tr|Nantan|tt|Нантан|uk|Нантан|vi|Nantan, Kyōto|war|Nantan, Kyoto|zh|南丹市|zh_classical|南丹市|zh_min_nan|Nantan-chhī|zh_yue|南丹市|qid=Q170421}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} under the old shrine-ranking system. The shrine crest is "tachibana" (mandarin orange). {{nihongo|'''Funai Shrine'''|船井神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tanba Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
The enshrined deities are the following seven pillars:
* '''{{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|de|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|it|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|ja|住吉三神|mni|ꯁꯨꯃꯤꯌꯣꯁꯤ ꯁꯟꯖꯤꯟ|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနတ်သုံးပါး|pl|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|simple|Sumiyoshi sanjin|zh|住吉三神|qid=Q1114013}}''' — the deities enshrined since the shrine's founding; a collective name for the following three:
** Sokotsutsuno-o-no-Mikoto
** Nakatsutsuno-o-no-Mikoto
** Uwatsutsuno-o-no-Mikoto
* '''{{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805|lt=Kasuga Four Deities}}''' — jointly enshrined in {{ill|Hōan|Q1194464|qid=Q1194464}} 1 ({{ill|1120|Q19542|qid=Q19542}}); a collective name for the following four:
** {{ill|Takemikazuchi|lt=Takemikazuchi|Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|qid=Q1502690|lt=Takemikazuchi-no-Mikoto}}
** {{ill|Futsunushi|lt=Futsunushi|Q1107286|qid=Q1107286|qid=Q1107286|lt=Futsunushi-no-Mikoto}}
** {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|Q2564508|qid=Q2564508|lt=Ame-no-Koyane-no-Mikoto}}
** {{ill|Himegami|Q22070227|qid=Q22070227}}

== History ==
== Founding ==
When {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} carried out the {{ill|Three Han Campaign|Q11249435|qid=Q11249435}}, she prayed to Sumiyoshi Myōjin, whereupon a ship appeared and the campaign succeeded. Because of this, a shrine was founded at this location to enshrine Sumiyoshi Myōjin.

About 500 meters northwest of the shrine there is a mound called "Oko no Mori" (Great Ancient Forest). It is said that the predecessor Sumiyoshi Shrine was originally located there, but was relocated to the present site of Kanomori (also "Kayamori")<ref>It is thought that the place name "Kanomori" (deer forest) arose because the Kasuga deity—associated with deer—was later jointly enshrined, giving rise to "Kasuga's deer forest," i.e. "Kanomori" ('Kyoto-fu no Chimei,' Funai Shrine entry).</ref> after a flood of the Ōi River in {{ill|Keiun|Q428753|qid=Q428753}} 2 ({{ill|705|Q23504|qid=Q23504}}).

The shrine and district name "Funai" is said to derive from the fact that this area was a mooring place (funai, "ship stop") for boats on the Ōi River ({{ill|Katsura River|Q2909307|qid=Q2909307|lt=Katsura River}}).

== General history ==
In the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Jinmyōchō}}, completed in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it is listed as "Funai Shrine" in {{ill|Funai District, Kyoto|ceb|Funai-gun|es|Distrito de Funai|fa|شهرستان فونای، کیوتو|fr|District de Funai|id|Distrik Funai, Kyōto|it|Distretto di Funai|ja|船井郡|ko|후나이군|my|ဖုနိုင်းဒေသ၊ ကျိုတို|pl|Powiat Funai|uk|Повіт Фунай|zh|船井郡|zh_yue|船井郡|qid=Q1078679}}, {{ill|Tanba Province|cs|Tanba (provincie)|de|Provinz Tamba|es|Provincia de Tanba|fa|ولایت تانبا|fr|Province de Tanba|gl|Provincia de Tanba|id|Provinsi Tamba|it|Tanba (provincia)|ja|丹波国|ko|단바국|lt|Tambos žemė|nl|Tamba (provincie)|pt|Província de Tanba|ru|Тамба (провинция)|simple|Tamba Province|sk|Tanba (provincia)|sr|Провинција Тамба|tr|Tamba (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тамба|zh|丹波國|zh_min_nan|Tanba-kok|qid=Q954511}}, and was ranked as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

According to shrine tradition, in {{ill|Ninna|Q1346317|qid=Q1346317}} 3 ({{ill|880|Q23618|qid=Q23618}}), the shrine buildings collapsed in a major earthquake and were rebuilt in {{ill|Anna (era)|Q1373003|qid=Q1373003}} 2 ({{ill|970|Q24047|qid=Q24047}}). In {{ill|Hōan|Q1194464|qid=Q1194464}} 1 ({{ill|1120|Q19542|qid=Q19542}}), the {{ill|Kasuga-no-Kami|Q11088805|qid=Q11088805}} was invited (kanjō) and jointly enshrined by {{ill|Fujiwara no Ieyasu|Q11623187|qid=Q11623187}}, who was then provincial governor of Tanba.

During the Edo period, the shrine was called "Kanomori Myōjin" or "Kasuga Daimyōjin"<ref>'Kyoto-fu no Chimei,' Funai Shrine entry.</ref>, and the shrine's stone lanterns bear the inscription "Kasuga Deity."

The main hall was destroyed by fire in {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 3 ({{ill|1832|Q7584|qid=Q7584}}) and rebuilt in Tenpō 6 ({{ill|1835|Q7597|qid=Q7597}}).

After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was ranked as a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}} under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine ranking system}}.

== Precinct ==
Among the shrine buildings, the main hall dates from {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 6 ({{ill|1835|Q7597|qid=Q7597}}) and the worship hall from {{ill|Kansei|Q1195131|qid=Q1195131}} 6 ({{ill|1794|Q7811|qid=Q7811}}). On the upper right of the inner worship hall, behind wire mesh, there is a horse ema said to have been made by {{ill|Hidari Jingorō|Q2668220|qid=Q2668220}}. It is said that every night the horse would escape from the ema to go drink water; because the bell around the horse's neck was noisy, wire mesh was installed.

Also in the precinct there is a five-tiered stupa called "Kainamori" (arm guard), said to enshrine the arm of {{ill|Abe no Sadato|Q3616500|qid=Q3616500}}. Many mounds and place names related to Sadatō survive in the area around the Kameoka Basin (see "{{ill|Abe no Sadato|Q3616500|qid=Q3616500}}").
